TRANS-PROVINCIAL
AIRLINES LTD.
SAFETY FEATURES OF YOUR DC-3
The design of this airplane,
the
continuing program of maintenance it
receives, and the experience of your
captain and crew make it unlikely that
you will ever need to use the built-in
safety features of the DC3. However, it
is sound practice for every traveller to
be acquainted with them.
YOUR SEAT BELT is designed for your
comfort and safety in case of turbulence.
Please keep it fastened whenever the seat
belt sign is illuminated. You may find it
convenient to leave your seat belt loosely
fastened at all times and pull it snug when
the sign is lighted.
EMERGENCY EXITS
are clearly marked on both sides of the cabin. Instructions for opening them are printed on
each of these exits. Do not open an emergency exit unless requested by a member of your crew.
ESCAPE WINDOWS OVER WINGS
LOCATIONS
1. Pull cover open.
2. Grasp RED handle and
turn.
3. Entire window is then
outward
4. Exit through window;
one leg first, then head
and shoulders, then the
other leg.
DOOR EXITS
WINDOW
EXIT
WINDOW
EXITS
Turn handle in direction of
arrow.
DOOR
EXIT
Push outward and down.
AFTER LEAVING AIRCRAFT
Proceed away from the aircraft in an orderly fashion to a safe distance in case of fire
- and keep together.
PLEASE READ OTHER SIDE

PLEASE DO NOT REMOVE THIS CARD FROM AIRPLANE
IMPORTANT INFORMATION
You are flying aboard an aircraft with
a Flight Crew which is thoroughly
trained
and
experienced. It
is
extremely unlikely that certain safety
facilities will be needed, but simply as
a precaution we would like to you to
be familiar with these features.
SEATBACKS
Ministry
of
Transportation
Regulations require your seatback to
be upright during taxi, take off and
landing.
NO SMOKING
When the "NO SMOKING" sign is off,
you
may
smoke cigarettes
while
seated
anywhere
in
the
Cabin.
Whenever the "NO SMOKING" sign
comes on, however, all cigarettes are
to be extinguished.
SEAT BELTS
Even if the "SEAT BELT" sign is
turned off in flight, it is recommended
that you
keep
your belt loosely
fastened, whenever you are in your
seat.
EMERGENCY LANDING
Remain calm and follow the instructions of your crew
at all times.
Loosen your collar and tie, remove glasses, hats, sharp
objects from clothing or pockets, and take off your
shoes. (Take shoes with you when leaving the aircraft).
Do not remove any other clothing.
Put your seat in an upright position, fasten your seat
belt securely
around your hips, and place both
together flat on the floor. Lean over, cross your arms,
hold your knees, and press your head into your folded
arms. Remain in this position until the aircraft comes to
a complete stop. (One or more impacts may follow the
initial impact).
Follow the crew's instructions when you leave the air.
craft.
RADIO RECEIVERS Radio receivers may not be operated while the aircraft is in
flight. They may act as miniature broadcasting stations and interfere with the aircraft's
navigation system, causing incorrect readings. Should you wish to operate any other elec.
tronic device, please notify the stewardess.
